name: East Asian Studies (Min)

rules.name: Area Courses Requirement
rules.desc:
Complete three area courses total, one in each of the following categories:

• Humanities

• History

• Social Sciences
Courses used toward the area courses requirement should have a thematic focus on East Asia and/or a region of East Asia and may be listed at any number level.
The listed courses are examples and not exhaustive; if uncertain whether a course fits into a specific category, please consult with the DUS and/or SSO.

rules.name: Three additional East Asia content courses (one numbered 100 or above)
rules.desc: Complete three additional content courses offered by the EALC Department core and/or courtesy/affiliated faculty in the literature, culture, linguistics, anthropology, archaeology, art and art history, history, philosophy, political science, religious studies, sociology, or another field as approved by the DUS, SSO, or advisor of East Asia, at least one of which must be a numbered at or above the 100-level. Courses may be selected from the lists of area courses, which contain examples, but are not exhaustive; see NavigateClasses under CHINA, JAPAN, KOREA, EALC, EASTASN, or other relevant departments. If uncertain whether a particular course fits into one of these categories, contact the SSO or DUS.

children.notes: Students who meet the language proficiency requirement through examination are required to take three language-oriented courses, as approved by the Director of Undergraduate Studies. gpa: Courses as well as their prerequisites must be completed with a grade point average (GPA) of 2.0 or better.
grading: All courses used in fulfillment of non-language requirements must be taken for letter grading and at least 3 units each.
policies:
The courses taken for the minor must add up to at least 20 units. Courses must be at least three units and taken with a letter grade to be counted towards the minor. Students are encouraged to distribute their coursework among at least three disciplines and two subregions in Asia. The subregions need not be traditionally defined.
All courses used in fulfillment of non-language requirements must be taught by a Stanford faculty member with a primary or courtesy/affiliated appointment in the Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures.
Eligible subject codes for courses used in fulfillment of requirements include: CHINA, CHINLANG, JAPAN, JAPANLNG, KOREA, KORLANG, EALC, EASTASN, ANTHRO, ARTHIST, ASNAMST, COMPLIT, DLCL, ETHICSOC, FEMGEN, FILMEDIA, GLOBAL, HUMSCI, HUMCORE, INTLPOL, INTNLREL, LINGUIST, MTL, PHIL, POLISCI, PUBLPOL, RELIGST, STS, SOC, TAPS, URBANST, OSPBEIJ, OSPHONGK, OSPKYOTO, OSPKYOCT, and/or other related departments.
The Director of Undergraduate Studies (DUS) may approve changes or substitutions to the fulfillment of requirements.
transferPolicy: External credit may be used in fulfillment of requirements with approval of the Director of Undergraduate Studies (DUS). External credit options include courses taught by the Bing Overseas Studies Program (BOSP), by other colleges or universities outside of Stanford, or internship or other educational experiences in East Asia.
reviewNotes: You take three area courses (one each in humanities, history and social sciences) and three more East Asia content courses (one numbered 100 or above), for at least 20 units. A subplan adds language proficiency (second year, or third year for East Asian Languages) and two area courses; its additional content courses are the same ones the minor asks for. Courses outside the language requirement must be letter graded and at least 3 units. You check by hand the content and subplan area courses, which must be taught by EALC core or affiliated faculty, the 2.0 GPA, and in the East Asian Languages subplan the three language-oriented courses the DUS approves when proficiency is shown by exam. The Bulletin does not say whether a subplan's two area courses may be among the three core area courses; here they are counted as two more courses.
